items.explanation: Two overlapping current oral anticoagulant orders: apixaban 5 mg BID (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic note documents switching rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starts apixaban, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and is still listed as a current medication, so the patient is on two anticoagulants concurrently.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) together with warfarin. Most recent ECG (2022-04-27, ECG 101515306) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with a markedly long QT of about 560-570 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was obtained at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (ECG 104882441, sinus rhythm, QTc about 370 ms), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). The start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window applies, due 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring ECG was obtained in time (it did, however, show QTc about 535 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order and first appearance in the current medication list). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, due 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm, QTc about 450 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (earliest order, first appearance in the current medication list). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not completed in time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (not present in the 2026-02-18 note, newly listed on 2026-08-01, order authored that day). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and the report was requested by fax but has not been received. Because that outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. As of the evaluation time (2026-09-24 12:00) no ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Paul Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the follow-up was completed within the required time.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (ordered 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication in the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation was therefore restarted/continued without the documented review of a major bleed; benefit versus bleeding risk (AF/atrial flutter with concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel) needs prescriber review.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 132-136/min with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and the nursing rhythm documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings and the note needs correction, with review of rate control and the current warfarin/AF management.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22). Dabigatran was last ordered in January 2025 and there is no current anticoagulant order; current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin only. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (heart failure/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and documented in cardiology clinic notes 2025-10-10 through 2026-06-27). No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the outpatient record; current medications are levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note the coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, which should be weighed when choosing an agent, but it does not remove the indication.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a history of cerebral infarction (embolic) with residual hemiparesis/ataxia. No anticoagulant order is present at any time in the record. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female), so oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an atrial premature beat, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (2025-07-19 through 2026-08-04) and a coded history of congestive/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy plus essential hypertension. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (heart failure, hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in a man, yet no anticoagulant is ordered (current medications famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) despite a coded problem of long-term anticoagulant use. Needs review of anticoagulation status.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 2026-07-18, valid to 2026-12-26; listed in the 2026-07-18 cardiology clinic note). His most recent ECG (2023-10-08, ECG 108018814) is sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT about 480-495 ms and Bazett QTc about 515 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which the QT monitoring memo requires the prescriber to review. Potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18) are low-normal. Note the 2024-05-14 note called the QT acceptable when escitalopram was started; re-measurement of this tracing gives QTc >=500 ms, and no ECG has been obtained since.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-07-12, valid to 2027-01-09). Most recent ECG (2025-11-24, ECG 106885519) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT about 525 ms and Bazett QTc about 535 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. QTc has risen from about 425 ms on the 2025-06-07 tracing (before amiodarone) to about 535 ms. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so electrolytes do not explain the prolongation. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07). Most recent ECG (2023-11-10, ECG 104821039) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT about 480-490 ms and Bazett QTc about 520 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. The 40 mg daily dose also exceeds the QT-related maximum recommended citalopram dose, so prescriber review and a repeat ECG are needed.

items.explanation: Two overlapping current oral anticoagulant orders: apixaban 5 mg BID (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic note documents switching rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starts apixaban, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and is still listed as a current medication, so the patient is on two anticoagulants concurrently.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) together with warfarin. Most recent ECG (2022-04-27, ECG 101515306) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with a markedly long QT of about 560-570 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was obtained at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (ECG 104882441, sinus rhythm, QTc about 370 ms), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). The start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window applies, due 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring ECG was obtained in time (it did, however, show QTc about 535 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order and first appearance in the current medication list). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, due 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm, QTc about 450 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (earliest order, first appearance in the current medication list). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not completed in time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (not present in the 2026-02-18 note, newly listed on 2026-08-01, order authored that day). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and the report was requested by fax but has not been received. Because that outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. As of the evaluation time (2026-09-24 12:00) no ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Paul Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the follow-up was completed within the required time.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (ordered 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication in the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation was therefore restarted/continued without the documented review of a major bleed; benefit versus bleeding risk (AF/atrial flutter with concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel) needs prescriber review.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 132-136/min with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and the nursing rhythm documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings and the note needs correction, with review of rate control and the current warfarin/AF management.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22). Dabigatran was last ordered in January 2025 and there is no current anticoagulant order; current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin only. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (heart failure/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and documented in cardiology clinic notes 2025-10-10 through 2026-06-27). No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the outpatient record; current medications are levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note the coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, which should be weighed when choosing an agent, but it does not remove the indication.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a history of cerebral infarction (embolic) with residual hemiparesis/ataxia. No anticoagulant order is present at any time in the record. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female), so oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an atrial premature beat, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (2025-07-19 through 2026-08-04) and a coded history of congestive/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy plus essential hypertension. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (heart failure, hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in a man, yet no anticoagulant is ordered (current medications famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) despite a coded problem of long-term anticoagulant use. Needs review of anticoagulation status.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 2026-07-18, valid to 2026-12-26; listed in the 2026-07-18 cardiology clinic note). His most recent ECG (2023-10-08, ECG 108018814) is sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT about 480-495 ms and Bazett QTc about 515 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which the QT monitoring memo requires the prescriber to review. Potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18) are low-normal. Note the 2024-05-14 note called the QT acceptable when escitalopram was started; re-measurement of this tracing gives QTc >=500 ms, and no ECG has been obtained since.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-07-12, valid to 2027-01-09). Most recent ECG (2025-11-24, ECG 106885519) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT about 525 ms and Bazett QTc about 535 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. QTc has risen from about 425 ms on the 2025-06-07 tracing (before amiodarone) to about 535 ms. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so electrolytes do not explain the prolongation. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07). Most recent ECG (2023-11-10, ECG 104821039) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT about 480-490 ms and Bazett QTc about 520 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. The 40 mg daily dose also exceeds the QT-related maximum recommended citalopram dose, so prescriber review and a repeat ECG are needed.

items.explanation: Two overlapping current oral anticoagulant orders: apixaban 5 mg BID (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic note documents switching rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starts apixaban, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and is still listed as a current medication, so the patient is on two anticoagulants concurrently.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) together with warfarin. Most recent ECG (2022-04-27, ECG 101515306) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with a markedly long QT of about 560-570 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was obtained at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (ECG 104882441, sinus rhythm, QTc about 370 ms), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). The start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window applies, due 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring ECG was obtained in time (it did, however, show QTc about 535 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order and first appearance in the current medication list). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, due 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm, QTc about 450 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (earliest order, first appearance in the current medication list). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not completed in time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (not present in the 2026-02-18 note, newly listed on 2026-08-01, order authored that day). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and the report was requested by fax but has not been received. Because that outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. As of the evaluation time (2026-09-24 12:00) no ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Paul Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the follow-up was completed within the required time.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (ordered 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication in the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation was therefore restarted/continued without the documented review of a major bleed; benefit versus bleeding risk (AF/atrial flutter with concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel) needs prescriber review.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 132-136/min with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and the nursing rhythm documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings and the note needs correction, with review of rate control and the current warfarin/AF management.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22). Dabigatran was last ordered in January 2025 and there is no current anticoagulant order; current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin only. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (heart failure/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and documented in cardiology clinic notes 2025-10-10 through 2026-06-27). No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the outpatient record; current medications are levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note the coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, which should be weighed when choosing an agent, but it does not remove the indication.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a history of cerebral infarction (embolic) with residual hemiparesis/ataxia. No anticoagulant order is present at any time in the record. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female), so oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an atrial premature beat, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (2025-07-19 through 2026-08-04) and a coded history of congestive/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy plus essential hypertension. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (heart failure, hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in a man, yet no anticoagulant is ordered (current medications famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) despite a coded problem of long-term anticoagulant use. Needs review of anticoagulation status.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 2026-07-18, valid to 2026-12-26; listed in the 2026-07-18 cardiology clinic note). His most recent ECG (2023-10-08, ECG 108018814) is sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT about 480-495 ms and Bazett QTc about 515 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which the QT monitoring memo requires the prescriber to review. Potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18) are low-normal. Note the 2024-05-14 note called the QT acceptable when escitalopram was started; re-measurement of this tracing gives QTc >=500 ms, and no ECG has been obtained since.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-07-12, valid to 2027-01-09). Most recent ECG (2025-11-24, ECG 106885519) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT about 525 ms and Bazett QTc about 535 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. QTc has risen from about 425 ms on the 2025-06-07 tracing (before amiodarone) to about 535 ms. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so electrolytes do not explain the prolongation. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07). Most recent ECG (2023-11-10, ECG 104821039) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT about 480-490 ms and Bazett QTc about 520 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. The 40 mg daily dose also exceeds the QT-related maximum recommended citalopram dose, so prescriber review and a repeat ECG are needed.

items.explanation: Two overlapping current oral anticoagulant orders: apixaban 5 mg BID (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic note documents switching rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starts apixaban, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and is still listed as a current medication, so the patient is on two anticoagulants concurrently.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) together with warfarin. Most recent ECG (2022-04-27, ECG 101515306) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with a markedly long QT of about 560-570 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was obtained at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (ECG 104882441, sinus rhythm, QTc about 370 ms), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). The start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window applies, due 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring ECG was obtained in time (it did, however, show QTc about 535 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order and first appearance in the current medication list). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, due 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm, QTc about 450 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (earliest order, first appearance in the current medication list). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not completed in time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (not present in the 2026-02-18 note, newly listed on 2026-08-01, order authored that day). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and the report was requested by fax but has not been received. Because that outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. As of the evaluation time (2026-09-24 12:00) no ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Paul Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the follow-up was completed within the required time.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (ordered 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication in the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation was therefore restarted/continued without the documented review of a major bleed; benefit versus bleeding risk (AF/atrial flutter with concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel) needs prescriber review.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 132-136/min with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and the nursing rhythm documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings and the note needs correction, with review of rate control and the current warfarin/AF management.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22). Dabigatran was last ordered in January 2025 and there is no current anticoagulant order; current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin only. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (heart failure/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and documented in cardiology clinic notes 2025-10-10 through 2026-06-27). No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the outpatient record; current medications are levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note the coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, which should be weighed when choosing an agent, but it does not remove the indication.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a history of cerebral infarction (embolic) with residual hemiparesis/ataxia. No anticoagulant order is present at any time in the record. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female), so oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an atrial premature beat, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (2025-07-19 through 2026-08-04) and a coded history of congestive/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy plus essential hypertension. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (heart failure, hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in a man, yet no anticoagulant is ordered (current medications famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) despite a coded problem of long-term anticoagulant use. Needs review of anticoagulation status.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 2026-07-18, valid to 2026-12-26; listed in the 2026-07-18 cardiology clinic note). His most recent ECG (2023-10-08, ECG 108018814) is sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT about 480-495 ms and Bazett QTc about 515 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which the QT monitoring memo requires the prescriber to review. Potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18) are low-normal. Note the 2024-05-14 note called the QT acceptable when escitalopram was started; re-measurement of this tracing gives QTc >=500 ms, and no ECG has been obtained since.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-07-12, valid to 2027-01-09). Most recent ECG (2025-11-24, ECG 106885519) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT about 525 ms and Bazett QTc about 535 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. QTc has risen from about 425 ms on the 2025-06-07 tracing (before amiodarone) to about 535 ms. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so electrolytes do not explain the prolongation. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07). Most recent ECG (2023-11-10, ECG 104821039) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT about 480-490 ms and Bazett QTc about 520 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. The 40 mg daily dose also exceeds the QT-related maximum recommended citalopram dose, so prescriber review and a repeat ECG are needed.

items.explanation: Two overlapping current oral anticoagulant orders: apixaban 5 mg BID (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic note documents switching rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starts apixaban, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and is still listed as a current medication, so the patient is on two anticoagulants concurrently.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) together with warfarin. Most recent ECG (2022-04-27, ECG 101515306) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with a markedly long QT of about 560-570 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was obtained at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (ECG 104882441, sinus rhythm, QTc about 370 ms), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). The start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window applies, due 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring ECG was obtained in time (it did, however, show QTc about 535 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order and first appearance in the current medication list). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, due 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm, QTc about 450 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (earliest order, first appearance in the current medication list). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not completed in time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (not present in the 2026-02-18 note, newly listed on 2026-08-01, order authored that day). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and the report was requested by fax but has not been received. Because that outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. As of the evaluation time (2026-09-24 12:00) no ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Paul Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the follow-up was completed within the required time.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (ordered 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication in the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation was therefore restarted/continued without the documented review of a major bleed; benefit versus bleeding risk (AF/atrial flutter with concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel) needs prescriber review.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 132-136/min with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and the nursing rhythm documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings and the note needs correction, with review of rate control and the current warfarin/AF management.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22). Dabigatran was last ordered in January 2025 and there is no current anticoagulant order; current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin only. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (heart failure/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and documented in cardiology clinic notes 2025-10-10 through 2026-06-27). No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the outpatient record; current medications are levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note the coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, which should be weighed when choosing an agent, but it does not remove the indication.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a history of cerebral infarction (embolic) with residual hemiparesis/ataxia. No anticoagulant order is present at any time in the record. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female), so oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an atrial premature beat, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (2025-07-19 through 2026-08-04) and a coded history of congestive/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy plus essential hypertension. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (heart failure, hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in a man, yet no anticoagulant is ordered (current medications famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) despite a coded problem of long-term anticoagulant use. Needs review of anticoagulation status.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 2026-07-18, valid to 2026-12-26; listed in the 2026-07-18 cardiology clinic note). His most recent ECG (2023-10-08, ECG 108018814) is sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT about 480-495 ms and Bazett QTc about 515 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which the QT monitoring memo requires the prescriber to review. Note the 2024-05-14 note called the QT acceptable when escitalopram was started; re-measurement of this tracing gives QTc >=500 ms, and no ECG has been obtained since.

Most recent ECG (2025-11-24, ECG 106885519) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT about 525 ms and Bazett QTc about 535 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. QTc has risen from about 425 ms on the 2025-06-07 tracing (before amiodarone) to about 535 ms. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so electrolytes do not explain the prolongation. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07). Most recent ECG (2023-11-10, ECG 104821039) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT about 480-490 ms and Bazett QTc about 520 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. The 40 mg daily dose also exceeds the QT-related maximum recommended citalopram dose, so prescriber review and a repeat ECG are needed.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) together with warfarin. Most recent ECG (2022-04-27, ECG 101515306) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with a markedly long QT of about 560-570 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was obtained at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (ECG 104882441, sinus rhythm, QTc about 370 ms), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). The start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window applies, due 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring ECG was obtained in time (it did, however, show QTc about 535 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order and first appearance in the current medication list). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, due 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm, QTc about 450 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (earliest order, first appearance in the current medication list). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not completed in time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (not present in the 2026-02-18 note, newly listed on 2026-08-01, order authored that day). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and the report was requested by fax but has not been received. Because that outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. As of the evaluation time (2026-09-24 12:00) no ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Paul Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the follow-up was completed within the required time.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (ordered 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication in the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation was therefore restarted/continued without the documented review of a major bleed; benefit versus bleeding risk (AF/atrial flutter with concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel) needs prescriber review.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 132-136/min with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and the nursing rhythm documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings and the note needs correction, with review of rate control and the current warfarin/AF management.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22). Dabigatran was last ordered in January 2025 and there is no current anticoagulant order; current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin only. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (heart failure/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and documented in cardiology clinic notes 2025-10-10 through 2026-06-27). No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the outpatient record; current medications are levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note the coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, which should be weighed when choosing an agent, but it does not remove the indication.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a history of cerebral infarction (embolic) with residual hemiparesis/ataxia. No anticoagulant order is present at any time in the record. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female), so oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an atrial premature beat, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (2025-07-19 through 2026-08-04) and a coded history of congestive/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy plus essential hypertension. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (heart failure, hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in a man, yet no anticoagulant is ordered (current medications famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) despite a coded problem of long-term anticoagulant use. Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (ordered 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication in the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 132-136/min with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and the nursing rhythm documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings and the note needs correction, with review of rate control and the current warfarin/AF management.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) together with warfarin. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

A 12-lead ECG was obtained at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (ECG 104882441, sinus rhythm, QTc about 370 ms), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the current medication list; order authored that day). Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order and first appearance in the current medication list). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies, due 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm, QTc about 450 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (earliest order, first appearance in the current medication list). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not completed in time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (not present in the 2026-02-18 note, newly listed on 2026-08-01, order authored that day). Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. Because that outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. As of the evaluation time (2026-09-24 12:00) no ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Paul Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the follow-up was completed within the required time.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (ordered 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication in the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation was therefore restarted/continued without the documented review of a major bleed; benefit versus bleeding risk (AF/atrial flutter with concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel) needs prescriber review.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 132-136/min with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and the nursing rhythm documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings and the note needs correction, with review of rate control and the current warfarin/AF management.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22). Dabigatran was last ordered in January 2025 and there is no current anticoagulant order; current medications are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin only. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (heart failure/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the outpatient record; current medications are levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note the coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, which should be weighed when choosing an agent, but it does not remove the indication.

No anticoagulant order is present at any time in the record. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female), so oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Her most recent ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an atrial premature beat, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (2025-07-19 through 2026-08-04) and a coded history of congestive/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy plus essential hypertension. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (heart failure, hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in a man, yet no anticoagulant is ordered (current medications famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) despite a coded problem of long-term anticoagulant use.
